A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and contain readable main text, figures, equations, and Appendices A–C. Reflow and figure relocation do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original synthetic-tree experiments, including training/test losses and learned parameter trajectories in Figures 4–7.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original synthetic-tree experiments and their results in Figures 4–7.

M1.justification: The single-head backward and two-head forward architectures, autoregressive procedures, trainable matrices, and training objective remain unchanged. The theorem-condition corrections do not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate backward and two-stage forward path-finding, training on perfect binary trees and testing on trees with varied depths, node counts, and branching.

E2.justification: Neither version reports an empirical comparison against external baseline methods. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 5 retains batch size 256, learning rates 1 and 0.2, backward settings m=4 and S=31, forward settings m=3 and S=25, and 1,024 test trees. Evaluation procedures and loss metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: The generalization checks and parameter-dynamics analyses in Figures 5 and 7 are retained. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary empirical analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Figures 4–7 retain the same curves without uncertainty bands.

E6.justification: Figures 4–7 contain identical loss curves and parameter trajectories, and Section 5 retains the same findings. No empirical result is added, removed, or corrected.

T1.justification: Theorem 2 replaces its second, duplicated b1 > 0 requirement with c1 > 0. Assumption 4 removes orthonormality requirements for stage tokens s_f and s_b, which are unused in backward reasoning. The proofs in Appendices A–C remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about shallow-transformer constructions, gradient-descent learning, head specialization, and generalization to unseen trees.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning coordinated attention heads, intermediate CoT steps, and learning generalizable path-finding rules remain unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability discussion is added.

D1.justification: Both versions provide the same one-hot embedding, SGD, tree-generation, and hyperparameter details. No implementation instructions, resource specifications, or code/data access information is added.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bachmann and Nagarajan (2024) on a similar next-token prediction task and Wang and Wang (2025) on group reasoning. It also explicitly mentions state tracking, while retaining the central research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited wording and citation-prose edits, updates the revision date, and adds a funding acknowledgment. Section order, overall narrative, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Text and equations reflow, and existing figures move: Figure 5 from page 12 to 13, Figure 7 from page 13 to 14, and Figure 8 from page 20 to 21. Their graphics and captions are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves formal precision by restoring the missing c1 > 0 condition in Theorem 2 and removing irrelevant stage-token requirements from Assumption 4. The added related-work references modestly improve contextual coverage. These are limited gains; the experimental evidence and appendix proofs are unchanged.
